lines: Paul Enright, ex-Viking Global and until recently Chairman of Fundamental Equities at pod shop Jain Global, argues stock returns are now driven more by multiple expansion and contraction than by earnings, which is far harder to systematize.

He contrasts the two models: a single-manager fund's unit of production is the exceptional idea, needing upfront quality control, while a multi-manager shop's unit is the portfolio, managed through after-the-fact risk control and leverage.
Enright says leverage, concentration and volatility cannot coexist, so managers must pick two and tightly limit the third.

On AI, he urges analysts to hand short-half-life work such as data gathering and consensus tracking to machines but do foundational company research themselves to build 'crystallized knowledge' and avoid cognitive debt.

He expects winning firms to be 'man plus machine' teams with fewer people per dollar of capital, blending public and private best ideas, and sees today's easiest alpha in battleground stocks whose multiples have moved far ahead of fundamentals.
podcast: Capital Allocators – Inside the Institutional Investment Industry
title: Single-Manager Hedge Funds, Pod Shops, and the Age of AI – Paul Enright (EP.527)
